accuracy.reason: All eight objectives are accurate and bounded: persistence/recovery, requirements-first selection, three record models, three specialized query types, overlapping capabilities, costs and partition-specific CAP. Primary followups verify graph, vector, spatial and document-transaction claims.

evidence.quote: Similarity does not prove exact equality or factual correctness.

mechanisms.reason: Shows how representation changes read assembly and coordinated updates, why indexes add write maintenance, how partition keys constrain access, how graph/vector queries work and why an isolated replica cannot answer freshly. DatabaseOverviewDiagram correctly maps product layouts and workloads.

evidence.quote: Embedding copies can simplify reads while adding updates to coordinate.

coherence.reason: Basic storage/network prerequisites suffice. Role and requirements frame model choices, specialized access and feature overlap; costs and network failures then inform the concluding selection method. Every card serves its objective without requiring another lesson.

evidence.quote: Requirements lead to a model, queries, and guarantees.

decisions.reason: Pairs benefits with storage/write/coordination/operating costs and insists on actual query measurements, guarantee checks and changed-requirement reconsideration. Avoids category rankings or compulsory multiple databases.

evidence.quote: A separate service can still make sense when workload needs or operating limits justify it.

clarity.reason: Defines access patterns, partition key, traversal and embeddings in plain language; data versus network partition is explicit. Product and path examples clarify real differences; assigned diagram and shared assets inspected, not rendered.

evidence.quote: This data partition is distinct from a network partition, which is a communication failure.

outcomes.reason: Defines managed persistent data and query/update consequences, qualifies storage/recovery, enumerates records, relationships, reads/updates, coupled rules, growth/latency and operational recovery; rejects category/brand guarantees.

Compares row/column relationships and joins, grouped documents with duplicate updates and known-key access; correctly explains query-shaped partition grouping versus network split, graph traversal and numerical-vector similarity limits.

Connects relational spatial/vector features to actual supported queries and measured workload, without feature-equivalence claims. Explains separate-store synchronization/operations, index maintenance, duplicate-update coordination and remote partial failures.

Defines replicated copies and live-node partition, derives stale-answer versus unavailable-operation conflict and scopes it to configuration/operation. Gives a requirements-to-capability-to-cost method with failure behavior and measurements that can change the choice; vendor and extra stores are optional.

sourceChecks.claim: PostgreSQL Concepts confirms managed relational tables and server clusters; previously verified WAL/backup documentation supports persistence dependent on recovery and hardware assumptions rather than universal loss prevention.

JSON Types confirms relational PostgreSQL stores/query-indexes JSON; MongoDB Transactions primary followup confirms multi-document transactions with configured guarantees. Access/operating requirements appropriately guide selection.

MongoDB data modeling documents nested fields, relationships, accessed-together storage and schema validation; PostgreSQL concepts/constraints corroborate tables and references. Direct key retrieval is a model definition, not an unqualified arbitrary-query promise.

Cassandra logical modeling requires tables around queries and partition/clustering keys determining grouping/access. Neo4j graph concepts confirms nodes, edges and traversal; pgvector primary documentation confirms distance-based exact/approximate search and recall/speed tradeoffs.

PostGIS documentation index and linked getting-started/manual pages lead to project overview confirming spatial storage/indexing/functions; pgvector project documents PostgreSQL vector extension. Neither establishes equal workload performance, as the lesson correctly cautions.

PostgreSQL index introduction confirms access-path benefit, planner choice and write maintenance. MongoDB modeling supports embedding tradeoffs; synchronization and partial-failure costs follow from additional copied/distributed state.

FoundationDB CAP page distinguishes all-node successful operations from practical system uptime, states completed-write consistency and partition-time choice; Gilbert/Lynch original paper verified in this review supports the isolated-reader derivation.

Concepts supplies database model context; final guidance synthesizes verified model, index and CAP limits into a measurement-based choice, without attributing benchmarks or universal product guarantees to that page.
